sections.section_title: Clinical Context and Presentation After Cardiac Surgery
sections.description: Frames the patient’s perioperative course, expected platelet dynamics after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), and the atypical early, progressive thrombocytopenia culminating in ischemic stroke.
subtopics: Baseline patient profile: elderly male with AF on apixaban; cardiac catheterization 1 week pre-op with 2000 U UFH
Index surgery: CPB with 45,000 U UFH; valve and aortic replacement, CABG; uneventful intraoperative course
Expected post-CPB thrombocytopenia versus observed pattern: mild drop on POD1, then progressive fall to 50 × 10^9/L by POD5 and nadir 13 × 10^9/L
Initiation of LMWH thromboprophylaxis and timing of switch to fondaparinux (POD5) due to falling platelets
Neurologic event: parietal ischemic stroke detected amid delirium and worsening thrombocytopenia
Epidemiology of HIT after cardiac surgery (0.5%–1.0%) and high thrombosis risk

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of HIT and Autoimmune HIT (aHIT)
sections.description: Explains immune mechanisms underlying classic HIT versus aHIT and links them to the patient’s laboratory phenotype, including heparin-independent platelet activation and partial Fc receptor blockade resistance.
subtopics: Classic HIT: PF4–heparin complexes, IgG antibodies, immune complex–mediated platelet activation via FcγRIIa clustering
aHIT spectrum: antibodies that activate platelets without heparin; clinical severity and persistence
Platelet activation cascade: FcγRIIa signaling, thrombin generation, consumptive coagulopathy; relevance to falling fibrinogen, rising D-dimer, schistocytes

Laboratory hallmarks: strong-positive PF4/polyanion ELISA; SRA profile with activation at low heparin (0.1–0.3 U/mL), inhibition at supratherapeutic heparin (100 U/mL), and activation at 0 U/mL indicating aHIT
Unique serologic feature in this case: partial resistance to FcγRIIa blockade by monoclonal antibody IV.3—implications for assay interpretation and disease severity
Immunologic kinetics: preoperative heparin exposure enabling earlier-onset HIT; evolution over months from heparin-independent to predominantly heparin-dependent reactivity

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning and Differential in Early Postoperative Thrombocytopenia
sections.description: Outlines a stepwise approach from presentation to diagnosis, emphasizing timing, exclusion of mimics, and nuanced interpretation of HIT assays in post-cardiac surgery patients.
subtopics: Timing as a diagnostic clue: early platelet fall before POD5 linked to recent pre-op UFH exposure
Applying clinical pretest probability (eg, timing, degree of fall, thrombosis) in the post-CPB setting
Differential diagnosis: postoperative hemodilution/consumption, infection/sepsis, DIC, TTP, post-transfusion purpura, drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia; reasons these were unlikely here

Laboratory evaluation: CBC with smear (no clumping, transient schistocytes later), hemolysis labs (haptoglobin high), coagulation panel (normal PT/PTT, high fibrinogen as acute phase), chemistries; cultures negative
Imaging for thrombosis: CT brain confirming parietal infarct
HIT testing strategy: PF4/polyanion ELISA (strong positive) and functional assay (SRA) interpretation
Interpreting an ‘indeterminate’ SRA when aHIT is present: activation at 0 U/mL heparin; partial inhibition with IV.3; avoiding false reassurance
Use of serial SRA to document evolution of antibody phenotype and support diagnosis

sections.section_title: Management of aHIT with Thrombosis and Severe Thrombocytopenia
sections.description: Details evidence-based treatment decisions in aHIT, including cessation of heparin, choice and adjustment of non-heparin anticoagulation, adjunctive immunomodulation, and monitoring strategies.
subtopics: Immediate actions: stop all heparin/LMWH; avoid catheter/heparin flushes

Non-heparin anticoagulation options: argatroban (short half-life, hepatic clearance) versus bivalirudin versus fondaparinux (AT-dependent anti-Xa); rationale for initial argatroban given stroke and bleeding risk
IVIG in aHIT: mechanism (FcγRIIa interference, anti-idiotype effects), dosing strategy (high-dose repeated due to poor initial response), expectations and variability
Assessing hypercoagulability control: serial fibrinogen, D-dimer, smear for schistocytes; recognizing consumptive coagulopathy despite anticoagulation
Switch to fondaparinux: indications (ease of use; concern for inadequate control), dosing and the role of antithrombin supplementation when AT activity is low
Neurologic considerations: balancing anticoagulation intensity after acute ischemic stroke with severe thrombocytopenia
Transition of care: duration of parenteral therapy, criteria to switch to oral anticoagulant (apixaban) once platelets recover and clinical stability achieved
Supportive care and avoidance strategies: platelet transfusions only for life-threatening bleeding or procedures; heparin allergy documentation; patient education

sections.section_title: Clinical Course, Laboratory Evolution, and Outcomes
sections.description: Tracks the patient’s response to therapy, laboratory trajectory, and serologic changes, connecting these to pathophysiology and treatment choices.
subtopics: Platelet trajectory: nadir at 13 × 10^9/L; gradual recovery to normal by POD62–87
Markers of consumptive coagulopathy during argatroban: falling fibrinogen to 2.49 g/L, rising D-dimer, transient schistocytes; improvement after switch to fondaparinux
Neurologic outcome: complete recovery despite early stroke
Serologic evolution: persistent strong SRA positivity for months; later profiles more typical of aHIT and eventual predominance of heparin-dependent activity
Long-term anticoagulation plan: completion of fondaparinux course and resumption of apixaban for AF
Follow-up considerations: duration of HIT antibody positivity, implications for future procedures and anticoagulant choices

sections.section_title: Key Lessons, Pitfalls, and Practical Takeaways
sections.description: Synthesizes teaching points for recognizing and managing aHIT in cardiac surgery patients, emphasizing timing, testing pitfalls, and therapeutic nuances.
subtopics: Early-onset HIT after cardiac surgery often signals preoperative heparin exposure—actively seek this history
Strong ELISA with atypical or ‘indeterminate’ SRA should raise suspicion for aHIT, especially if there is 0 U/mL heparin activation or partial FcγRIIa blockade
Do not rely on normal PT/PTT or high fibrinogen in early postoperative period to exclude hypercoagulability; track trends and D-dimer
Severe thrombocytopenia with thrombotic complications and consumptive features suggests aHIT; consider early IVIG and be prepared for variable responses
Choose non-heparin anticoagulants tailored to bleeding risk, organ function, and control of hypercoagulability; consider AT repletion when using fondaparinux
Document heparin as contraindicated; plan future procedures with non-heparin alternatives and alert teams
Serial functional testing can document antibody phenotype evolution and support ongoing management decisions
